cohorts.summary: New players encounter severe matchmaking imbalances against veteran setups, long queue times, and technical launch failures.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that new players are placed into matches against veterans equipped with high-tier gear or tanks, leading to immediate elimination.

citations.review_text: I have this on my Xbox and decided to download this on my pc cause it's fun to play....... but now the only way to advance in reputation is by getting a kill................. YET... you get put into matches with people who have legendary tier equipment while if you're just starting off with only the basic **** unless new players decided to spend actual money in order to survive otherwise you're killed within 2-3 seconds of first coming into contact with an enemy

Fun game but only being given a rust bucket and expected to fight people with tanks and laser cannons isn't fun, the microtransactions are insane and I can't possibly see justifying how much they expect you to spend on the vehicles in this game, it may be free to play but there are similar games that are more fun and not as expensive. I played this mostly to play it with my friend but the game doesnt let you play together until you're both level 10, I played this for over an hour an only got to level 5, the matches take like 5 minutes to find one, and even still most of the slots are filled with bots, the players that do show are people that have hundreds of hours and maxed out tank vehicles that can one shot you, the weapons the game gives you at the start have no hope of destroying them. The game doesnt seem to separate lower level players from higher levels either, so you either play against bots that run into walls the whole fight or you fight high level players that sit in one place and shoot because you can't kill them an they only need to hit you once, there is no skill involved. The games building is interesting and fun, but your very limited on what you have at the start, the game constantly has pop ups trying to get you to buy passes and packs, casually pushing a $65 pack on my screen with less then an hour of game time. The gameplay was fun, the driving felt good, the guns felt fun, they nailed the physics an such pretty well, I could see this being a fun game if the progress wasn't so pushed towards spending money in order to compete normally with other players.
Even if you can find a game when you first start, you will die immediately. Not new player friendly at all

You'll just end up forced to buy lots of premium coin packs and car DLCs as you waste more of your precious time on this game and start to regret.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a singleplayer campaign or story mode that is boring.

citations.review_text: the campaign / story mode thing was actually extremely boring

Since apparently they killed the Australian servers a few years back every game is 200+ ping, with input lag on every action, even just moving your guns around, not even the singleplayer PVE campaign they've added is spared. 

I guess there weren't enough players for them to justify keeping the servers open, but maybe there would've be more players if their monetization and management of the game wasn't so terrible.

The Game is not good because of way to many reasons. Listen i love the Fighting, Car Building(definitly a 10/10 feature). but everything else ? is pretty bad. the matchmaking is horrible. pvp feels like getting bullied because you get locked into a room with a 100kg dude but im only allowed to be 50kg ? that is just unfair and it feels trash to win one round and the next be completly destroyed and not even get normal ressources for that ? next is the game hasnt really changed since 8 years ago... i can tell you how much money making soul sucking in game items you can buy but any REAL, emotionale engaging awesome action oriented additions ? nah its the same game just more items. next is the company Gaijin... they are making live service games, i get it why they are trying to sell you stuff etc. but honestly its just not enjoyable because of stuff like this. the game favors pay to win extremely, doesnt care about properly balancing matches so they feel fair and engaging. honestly i feel like if they made this into a singeplayer/multiplayer without their studpid transactions it could have been a much better game and actually be relevant in 20 years when nobody is playing it anymore, like most live service stuff. the story is also horribly sad and poorly made. its drive around, see this conversation, fight this enemy, thats it. how can you put to little into something ? it makes me furious when i see such cool mechanics like the car building get wasted on such a live service garbage. im ranting but honestly just try it out. if you are a liveless loser who wants to grind 2000 hours to have a somewhat normal arsenal of items so the experimenting feels fun and you want to learn the ingame trading against other players so you can have a few coins to buy stuff. then go ahead. i love the concept, but the publisher is very anti player and pro money which is the very very sickness which is rotting gaming as a whole.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game lacks cross-progression, preventing players from transferring accounts and progress from consoles to PC.

citations.review_text:
30 hours on PC and 500+ hours and countless packs bought on console. 

Above is another reason I can't recommend the game, no transfer of your bought packs despite they are the exact same. 

The game is grindy as hell and it keeps locking fun events behind timelocks. 
On top of that the packs are insanely expensive compared to what you get but I feel like they push you to buy it unless you wanna spend days grinding your way up to a decent power score.
Mind you the game is fun, building is great and the matches are fun although they are mostly bots. 

This game could be amazing with a serious revamp, sadly it won't happen due to this company having been working like this for years.

The game balance is completely broken; certain weapons outclass everything else, making it a pure Pay-to-Win experience. To progress or get decent weapons, you are forced to either spend an insane amount of time grinding for ages or pay real money for Battle Passes. There is no respect for the player's time.
​Additionally, it is frustrating that there is no Cross-Progression. As someone who played on console, I cannot transfer my account and progress to PC. Being forced to start from zero on a different platform is unacceptable in today's gaming standards.

citations.review_text: its the pay to grind game, unbalanced newest paid for weapons are way op then get smashed to the ground by the time an average player can get it. everythings expensive. and if a new player, its extremely hard to get uranium to craft top weapons needed for clan wars. no relic wepons? no way to get them then for most part. and just constant switching of weapon stats from dominating to useless and flipping same weapons. then if you like a weapon as well theyve completely changed lots of em as well making it a product you didnt even buy.

I play this game because of its creative potential, and as a beta player, I have played enough of the game to be able to make just about anything I want. Any playstyle, any aesthetic, anything. For these purposes there is no other game like Crossout. Robocraft was nowhere near as satisfying to actually LOOK at as Crossout can be for a player with enough parts and decor variety to bring their vision to life. YES, for those of you wondering, that means that the combat is, to me, only one component of my enjoyment. Crossout is an Art Game.

However, the game has entered the end-stage F2P lifecycle, and the scummy business practices designed to cater to whales have metastasized into game direction. There are good deals relative to Gaijin's other products, but without buying SOMETHING, the game is a traditional gaijin grind where you play for hours and hours to grind out highish tier equipment, except unlike War Thunder, that grind in Crossout nets you a single weapon, a single cabin, or a single piece of equipment. There are free packs that anyone can obtain (completely free) which give you a jump-start on the game, but past that, most players end up using bland components for far, far too long. There are no social gamemodes outside of Bedlam (free-for-all with no rewards) which is full of endgame players looking for new players to bully, and in general, player count has dropped to an admittedly stable base of longtime players. New players aren't very common, and they rarely stick around because of the lack of commitment to their retention from the devs/publishers.

If I lost my account, I would not return to Crossout. Since that hasn't happened, I will usually play one or two months of Crossout as my only video game, because it scratches an itch no other game can.

It's a shame that I can't recommend this game, as it's probably my favorite game of all time, although some others (FNV first time, Skyrim first time, Minecraft with friends, Halo ODST) are also naturally in…

The Bad:
